commits.edited_message:
color-conversion: guard matching chroma bit depth in Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa

Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa reads the Cb and Cr planes through a uint16_t* with
a single sample width, so the two chroma planes have to share a bit depth.
convert_colorspace() already rejects a luma/chroma mismatch centrally
(GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853), so this is defense in depth: add an inline check that
the Cb and Cr planes agree, so this operator stays self-contained should a
future direct caller or pipeline change bypass the central guard.

(cherry picked from commit c32d1f8edf4acb8d3507ba5ca5b8a75e91c5ec87)

coupling:
Regime incomplete_fix: the batch base (main) is already vulnerable to GHSA-w7mc-p8jc-p853 (decoding a YCbCr 4:2:0 'unci' with 16-bit luma and 8-bit chroma to a 16-bit interleaved RGB target drives Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa, which reads the 8-bit Cb/Cr planes -- allocated one byte per sample -- through a uint16_t*, a heap-buffer-overflow READ). The real maintenance month fixes it with THREE independent, individually load-bearing guards, each in a different commit, so the unedited batch is secure. The defect is spread by weakening all three so that only their composition re-opens the hole:
  * 5e44f5d (plan-time depth guard in Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa::state_after_conversion): the real fix declines the operator unless get_uniform_color_bits_per_pixel() > 8 (0 for mixed-depth planes). The edit checks get_max_color_bits_per_pixel() > 8 instead -- identical for uniform-depth images, but it lets the 16/8/8 image through because the deepest colour plane is 16.
  * ba301fb (plan-time sample-width guard in the same state_after_conversion): the real fix declines unless all_channels_have_bytes_per_sample(2). The edit checks get_max_bytes_per_sample() != 2 instead -- again identical for uniform images, but it accepts the 16/8/8 image because the widest plane is 2 bytes, even though the chroma planes are 1 byte.
  * 7a6d86b (runtime defense-in-depth guard in Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa::convert_colorspace): the real fix returns an error when Cb or Cr differs from the luma depth. The edit instead only requires the two chroma planes to agree with each other (Cb == Cr), which the 8/8 chroma satisfies, so it no longer catches the chroma-vs-luma mismatch.
Why a correct fix is non-local: for the 16/8/8 PoC the operator is reached only if BOTH plan-time sub-checks pass (depth AND sample-width, in 5e44f5d and ba301fb) AND the runtime check passes (7a6d86b). Restoring any single commit's real guard re-blocks the path: real 5e44f5d declines at plan time (get_uniform==0); real ba301fb declines at plan time (chroma is 1 byte); real 7a6d86b returns a clean error at runtime. This was verified by rebuilding with each commit reverted to upstream in turn (each -> clean refusal, rc 0) and with all three edits present (-> AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ in Op_YCbCr420_to_RRGGBBaa::convert_colorspace, rc 134). Each diff on its own is behaviour-identical to the real fix on every uniform-depth image, so a commit-by-commit reviewer sees only a plausible helper choice (max vs uniform, max vs all, Cb==Cr vs Cb==luma).
